sam_runtime: Heads up — noticed a regression on Mixtral MoE serving after the recent kernel bump + RoPE-scaling tweak. P50 token latency +12%, top-k routing CPU up ~30%, expert cache miss rate jumped from 2.1% -> 9.7% in prod canary.

oliver_perf: ugh. which kernel bump and exact config changes?

sam_runtime: kernel: gemm-v2.4.0 (was v2.3.1). RoPE scale factor drifted from 1.0 -> 0.98 in the rollout (attempt to reduce fp overflows). batching heuristic: pref_batch_tokens lowered from 64 -> 48. router: topk=4, temp=1.0. expert_parallelism configured to 8.

maria_engineering: do we have traces or small flamegraphs? need p50/p99 and a breakdown by module.

sam_runtime: quick snapshot from runtime-trace (sampled):
```
serving.moe.router         CPU  32%   (was 18%)
serve.kernel.gemm         GPU    58%   (similar)
kv.cache.miss_rate        9.7%   (was 2.1%)
batch.size                9.2 reqs (avg)  (was 12.5)
avg.latency/token         12.4ms (was 11.0ms)
p99.latency/token         48.1ms (was 41.0ms)
```

oliver_perf: batch size drop explains extra router ops per token. why did batch size shrink? the pref_batch_tokens change is suspect.

sam_runtime: theory: RoPE scaling tweak changed token distribution slightly (longer generation steps distribution), batching logic prefers smaller windows due to increased sequence-length variance -> more partial batches. also kernel v2.4 changed head-tiling path which may be worse for Mixtral head/kv dims.

maria_engineering: that matches: Mixtral uses 64 heads with kv_dim=64; the new GEMM kernel picks a vectorized path that doesn't align well with our head stride, causing underutilized tensor cores for small-ish batches. Need kernel counters.

oliver_perf: propose experiments (canary):
- revert gemm -> v2.3.1
- restore pref_batch_tokens=64
- sweep router temp [0.7,0.85,1.0] and topk [4,6,8]
- try expert_parallelism [8,12,16] to spread router CPU
- bump KV cache TTL and enable prefix caching

sam_runtime: started first two already. canary id: canary-2024-08-12-7. revert kernel deployed at 1745001280. pref_batch_tokens=64 rolled 1745001290.

ci-bot: deploy(canary-2024-08-12-7) succeeded :white_check_mark:

maria_engineering: I'll hook kernel perf counters (L2 miss, warp occupancy, tensor-core utilization) and run a 2k-request sample to compare v2.3.1 vs v2.4.0.

sam_runtime: perf hook added, sampling 2k requests now. trace link: https://telemetry.redwood/prod/canary-2024-08-12-7/trace

oliver_perf: early numbers after revert?

sam_runtime: preliminary: p50 token latency back to roughly +1% (vs baseline) after revert, router CPU down to ~20%, KV miss rate dropped to 3.0%. p99 still slightly elevated, need sweep.

maria_engineering: good. still want to validate router knobs: sweeping temp/topk/expert_parallelism and measure cost/latency/quality tradeoffs. I'll run an automated sweep and collect CSVs + flamegraphs.

sam_runtime: suggested run: temp=0.85 + topk=6 + expert_parallelism=12 looks promising (routes a bit more diversely, reduces per-expert thrash). if that reduces miss rate and p50 < baseline we can promote.

oliver_perf: also we should fix the batching heuristic long-term: implement sequence-length bucketing so batches maintain useful size despite RoPE-induced seq_len variance. current single-window heuristic is brittle.

maria_engineering: agree — I'll prototype a bucketed batching that groups by recent seq_len percentiles and keeps pref_batch_tokens per-bucket. should keep average batch size stable.

sam_runtime: runbook for next 48h:
- maria_engineering: run sweep + upload CSVs/flamegraphs to thread
- oliver_perf: monitor autoscaler and prepare fallback configs for capacity/cost pacing
- sam_runtime: keep canary warm, watch regression dashboards and update here with final numbers

ci-bot: created ticket PERF-4279: https://jira.redwood/browse/PERF-4279

sam_runtime: thanks -- adding :eyes: and will post final sweep results tonight.

oliver_perf: thx everyone :thumbsup:
